title: 🇮🇳 US Tariff on India: 17% or 25%? Rupee, Tata Sons & More | StickBiz Brief | 26 Nov 2026

segments.headline: Mixed start, weaker rupee · 17% or 25%: deal decides
segments.cap: India faces a US tariff of 17% with a trade deal, or up to 25% without one. The rupee, Tata Sons and Adani bonds are also in focus.
segments.tts: [excited] India faces a US tariff of seventeen percent with a trade deal, or up to twenty-five percent without one. The rupee, Tata Sons and Adani bonds are also in focus.

banner: It all hinges on a deal

segments.headline: Mixed start, weaker rupee
segments.cap: Sensex and Nifty were mixed in morning trade on Thursday. The Sensex was up 0.17% at 84,076.82, while the Nifty was down 0.10% at 25,793.20. The rupee slipped 20 paise to 92.40 against the dollar. Oil above $95 a barrel and the US tariff plan raised dollar demand, traders said. Still, the rupee has recovered nearly 5% from its record low close of 96.88 on 8 October.
segments.tts: [excited] Sensex and Nifty were mixed in morning trade on Thursday. The Sensex was up zero point one seven percent at eighty-four thousand seventy-six. eighty-two, while the Nifty was down zero point one zero percent at twenty-five thousand seven hundred ninety-three. twenty. The rupee slipped twenty paise to ninety-two point four zero against the dollar. Oil above ninety-five dollars a barrel and the US tariff plan raised dollar demand, traders said. Still, the rupee has recovered nearly five percent from its record low close of ninety-six point eight eight on the eighth of October.

segments.headline: 17% or 25%: deal decides
segments.cap: The US has proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners, India included. India would face 17% if a trade deal is signed, and up to 25% without one. With a deal, Bangladesh would face 18%, and Vietnam and China 20%. Think tank GTRI says the two-rate design is a way to push countries into deals. India rejects the claim of excess capacity and says it wants an early trade deal.
segments.tts: [excited] The US has proposed new tariffs on fourteen trading partners, India included. India would face seventeen percent if a trade deal is signed, and up to twenty-five percent without one. With a deal, Bangladesh would face eighteen percent, and Vietnam and China twenty percent. Think tank GTRI says the two-rate design is a way to push countries into deals. India rejects the claim of excess capacity and says it wants an early trade deal.

segments.headline: Tata Sons board showdown
segments.cap: The Tata Sons board will meet on 30 November, after the date moved from 26 November. The RBI told Tata Sons on 16 November to follow listing rules for large finance companies. Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata wants his own issues discussed first, and prefers a plan to keep Tata Sons private. Tata Trusts is also taking the chairman's reappointment to the Bombay High Court.
segments.tts: [excited] The Tata Sons board will meet on the thirtieth of November, after the date moved from the twenty-sixth of November. The RBI told Tata Sons on the sixteenth of November to follow listing rules for large finance companies. Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata wants his own issues discussed first, and prefers a plan to keep Tata Sons private. Tata Trusts is also taking the chairman's reappointment to the Bombay High Court.

segments.headline: Adani plans public bonds
segments.cap: Adani Enterprises and Adani Power plan public bond sales to raise at least ₹2,000 crore, according to people familiar. One offer is aimed for the end of December and the other for March. The terms are not final. Indian firms have raised ₹4,840 crore through public bonds this fiscal year, against ₹11,340 crore in all of the last one.
